title: Partial Dentures
meta_title: Partial Dentures in Alexandria, VA | West Alexandria Dental Care
meta_description: Removable partial dentures at West Alexandria Dental Care: metal framework versus flexible, how clasps hold, when a partial beats a bridge or implants.
intro: A partial denture replaces several missing teeth on a removable plate that clips onto the teeth you still have. It is the most economical way to fill multiple gaps, it needs no surgery, and a well-designed one is stable enough to eat with comfortably. It is also the option most often done badly, so the design matters.

sections.heading: How a partial stays in
body: A partial denture rests on the gums and is held by clasps or clips that grip the remaining teeth. The teeth it clasps are chosen carefully: they need to be healthy, well supported in bone, and positioned so the partial seats in one direction and cannot rock. Rests, small extensions that sit on the chewing surfaces of those teeth, stop the partial sinking into the gum under chewing load. Get that design right and a partial feels secure; get it wrong and it moves with every bite.

sections.heading: When a partial is the right choice
items: Several teeth are missing, in different places, so a single bridge would not reach.
The remaining teeth are not strong enough to carry a bridge.
Implants are not advisable for medical reasons, or not wanted.
Budget or insurance favors a removable option now, with implants possible later.
Teeth are still being lost and the plan will change; a partial can have teeth added.

items.title: Planning the design
items.body: Which teeth will carry clasps, where rests will sit, and whether any of those teeth need small adjustments or crowns first to give the partial a proper seat.

items.title: Impressions
items.body: Precise impressions of both arches and a bite record. For a metal framework, the laboratory casts the frame first.

items.title: Framework try-in
items.body: The metal frame is tried in alone to check that it seats fully and the clasps grip without pressure on the gum. Then the teeth are set in wax for a second try-in.

items.title: Delivery and adjustments
items.body: The finished partial is fitted, the bite checked and the clasps tuned. Expect a follow-up or two for sore spots; they are normal and quick to fix.

sections.heading: Living with a partial
body: Speech settles within days. Eating starts soft and builds up; chewing on both sides keeps it stable. It comes out at night and is brushed with a denture brush and soap, never toothpaste, which scratches it. The clasped teeth need particularly careful brushing and flossing, because plaque collects under the clasps and those teeth are the ones you cannot afford to lose.

A partial can be converted later. If a clasped tooth is eventually lost, a tooth can be added to a metal partial. If you later decide on implants, a partial can serve as the temporary while they heal, or implants with attachments can hold it far more securely.

sections.heading: Compare it with a bridge and implants
sections.body: A partial is removable and the most economical. A bridge is fixed but needs sound neighboring teeth and only spans short gaps. Implants are fixed, spare the neighbors and keep the bone, at higher cost and with surgery. Our decision guide sets them side by side.

faqs.a: On a metal partial, clasps on back teeth are hidden. On front teeth they can be visible when you smile widely; the design tries to place them where they are least seen, and a flexible partial or a precision attachment can hide them altogether at some cost in support.
No. The gums and the clasped teeth need the rest, and sleeping in any denture raises the risk of sore, infected tissue and decay on the clasped teeth.

faqs.q: How long will it take to get used to?
faqs.a: Most people are comfortable within two to three weeks. The first week feels bulky and affects speech; reading aloud helps. Sore spots are adjusted, not endured.
Usually as a major restoration at a percentage, with limits on replacement frequency. We check your benefits and give you the cost in writing before the impressions.

cta.heading: Fill the gaps without losing what you have.
cta.body: A partial depends on good design around your remaining teeth. Book a consultation and we will plan one that stays put, with the cost beside the alternatives.
